On the procedure for admitting graduates who have successfully completed technical colleges to bachelor’s degree programmes of higher education institutions on the basis of an interview
REGULATION
Chapter 1. General provisions

1. This Regulation establishes the procedure for admitting graduates who have successfully completed technical colleges (hereinafter — graduates) to continue their studies from the 2nd year of higher education institutions, in bachelor’s degree programmes corresponding to their field, without entrance examinations, through an individual interview.

This Regulation does not apply to higher military and higher paramilitary educational institutions, Tashkent State University of Law, foreign and non-state higher education organisations operating in Uzbekistan and their branches.

The list of bachelor’s degree programmes corresponding to their field in which graduates may continue their studies from the 2nd year of higher education institutions is approved by the Ministry of Higher and Secondary Specialised Education of the Republic of Uzbekistan.
Graduates are admitted to the 2nd year of bachelor’s degree programmes without entrance examinations, through an individual interview, on a paid-contract basis.
The tuition fee under the paid-contract form of study is set on the basis of the costs of training one student.

4. Graduates who have successfully completed a technical college are those whose grades at the end of the academic semesters throughout their studies at the technical college are “5 (excellent)” and “4 (good)”, provided that at least 50 percent of the grades (at least 85 percent for medical higher education institutions) are “5 (excellent)”.

Starting from the 2021/2022 academic year, the procedure for admitting graduates to bachelor’s degree programmes of higher education institutions without entrance examinations, through an individual interview, applies for two years from the year of graduation from the technical college.

Persons who do not belong to the above category and who graduated from a technical college more than two years ago are admitted to bachelor’s degree programmes of higher education institutions, when they express a wish to study, in accordance with the general procedure.
5. Graduates are admitted by interview to bachelor’s degree programmes corresponding to their field according to the scheme in Annex 1 to this Regulation.
Chapter 2. Acceptance of documents

6. Every year an admission commission is formed by order of the rector of the higher education institution (director of the branch) for admitting graduates to the 2nd year of the higher education institution.
The rector of the higher education institution (director of the branch) is the chairman of the admission commission.
Every year, from July 5 to July 25, graduates register online through the official website of the Ministry of Higher and Secondary Specialised Education of the Republic of Uzbekistan.
When registering for bachelor’s degree programmes of higher education institutions, graduates are required to enter their personal data into the system and upload the following documents:
a copy of the passport or ID card;
a document on graduation from the technical college and a copy of its appendix.
The registration of graduates is coordinated by the Ministry of Higher and Secondary Specialised Education through the Ministry’s official website.

The documents uploaded to the system by graduates who registered online are examined by the admission commissions of higher education institutions every year by August 5, and the results of the examination are communicated to the applicants through their personal accounts.

If the documents submitted by a graduate are found to be forged, the graduate is excluded from the interview (or, if this is discovered after admission, from the student body), and the documents are sent to the law enforcement authorities in the established order.
Chapter 3. Organisation and conduct of the interview
11. Every year by August 10, the rector of the higher education institution (director of the branch) forms, by his or her order, a separate Interview Commission for each field of study.

The Interview Commission is formed of at least 9 members and includes responsible officials of organisations that are the main employers of personnel and of ministries and departments to which the higher education institution is subordinate, a highly qualified teacher of the technical college in the relevant field, and, as a rule, a professor-teacher of the higher education institution in the relevant field.

12. The interview for admitting graduates who have successfully completed technical colleges to higher education institutions is held under full video surveillance, and the process is broadcast online, with sound, to a separate waiting area for parents and observers.

Responsibility for ensuring that the interview is held under full and high-quality video surveillance, and that the video recordings are stored at the higher education institution for at least three years, is assigned personally to the rector of the higher education institution (director of the branch).

13. The interview for admitting graduates to higher education institutions is held every year from August 10 to August 25, within the period set by the higher education institution, provided that at least two thirds of the members of the Interview Commission take part.
The dates of the interview are announced on the official website of the higher education institution at least one week before the interviews begin.
Representatives of the public may also be involved in the interview as impartial observers.

14. Graduates who do not come to the interview within the set time limits are not given a repeat interview for that academic year and are not admitted to the 2nd year of a bachelor’s degree programme of the higher education institution.

If a graduate cannot take part in the interview, or does not take part, for a valid reason (illness, a business trip or the death of a family member, confirmed by a document), he or she must apply to the admission commission formed at the higher education institution no later than three days after the date of the interview. For graduates of this category an additional interview is held within one week after the interview process has been fully completed.
15. During the interview, each graduate is asked four questions in total, one on each of the following topics:
understanding the essence and importance of the reforms being carried out in the country in the graduate’s field;
motivation in choosing the bachelor’s degree programme (understanding the essence and social importance of the profession, a steady interest in it);

personal and professional qualities (ability to study, practical activity in solving professional tasks, discipline, solidarity, responsibility, degree of independence in decision-making, personal achievements, as well as the ability to work on oneself and creativity);
knowledge and professional skills in the field of the chosen bachelor’s degree programme.
The maximum total score that can be obtained is 100 points.
The criteria for assessing these questions are developed and approved by the relevant higher education institution and published on its official website.
16. The questions are developed by the admission commission of the higher education institution and approved by the chairman of the admission commission.
Responsibility for ensuring that the questions correspond to the topics provided for in paragraph 15 of this Regulation is assigned to the chairman of the admission commission.

17. During the interview, each member of the Interview Commission is given a graduate’s interview result record sheet (hereinafter — the interview result record sheet) in the model form according to Annex 2 to this Regulation.
The members of the Interview Commission award points on the interview result record sheet according to the result of the interview with each graduate and sign it.

18. After the interview in a given field of study (group) is completed, the points on the interview result record sheets filled in by the members of the Interview Commission are counted, and on this basis the final result record sheet of the interview with the graduate (hereinafter — the final result record sheet of the interview) in the model form according to Annex 3 to this Regulation is filled in and approved by the Interview Commission.

According to the final result record sheet of the interview approved by the Interview Commission, an applicant is considered to have passed the interview when the average of the points given by the participating members of the Interview Commission is 67 points or higher.
The list of those who passed the interview in a given field of study (group) is read out to the applicants on the same day.
19. During the interviews, an appeal commission is formed at the higher education institution to consider appeals in the established order.

Appeals are accepted within 24 hours from the time the interview results are announced, directly at the higher education institution in writing or online through the official website of the Ministry of Higher and Secondary Specialised Education, and are considered by the appeal commission on the basis of the video recording within one to three days, depending on the number of applicants.

Information on those recommended for admission as students according to the interview results is submitted by the rector of the higher education institution (director of the branch) to the ministry or department to which it is subordinate within three days from the date the results are announced.
The interview result record sheets and the final result record sheets of the interview of the Interview Commission are stored at the higher education institution for three years.

The members of the Interview Commission are paid out of the extra-budgetary paid-contract funds of the higher education institution, under the conditions of hourly pay established for conducting classes with students of higher education institutions.
Chapter 4. Admission as students on a paid-contract basis

According to the final result record sheet of the interview approved by the Interview Commission, graduates are recommended by the rector of the higher education institution (director of the branch) for admission as students to continue their studies from the 2nd year of the bachelor’s degree programme corresponding to their field.

The general list of those recommended for admission as students is published on the website of the higher education institution one day after the interview process has been fully completed, and from that day the admission commission of the higher education institution issues to them paid-contract forms of the established model.
Payment for those recommended for admission as students is made every year within the periods specified in the contract.
The terms of the contract, the rights and obligations of the parties and the procedure for their implementation are determined in accordance with legislation.

26. According to the final result record sheet of the interview approved by the Interview Commission, those recommended for admission as students are admitted, after fulfilling the paid-contract conditions within the set periods, to the 2nd year of a particular bachelor’s degree programme by order of the rector of the higher education institution.
Chapter 5. Final provisions
Disputes arising in the application of this Regulation are resolved in the manner established by legislation.
Persons guilty of violating the requirements of this Regulation are liable in accordance with legislation.
